name: Motion for a resolution (as a whole)
title: MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on supporting the United Kingdom accession to the Convention of 2 July 2019 on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Judgments in Civil or Commercial Matters
part_text:
The European Parliament supports the United Kingdom joining a global agreement on recognising court judgments in civil and commercial matters. If the EU accepts the UK's accession, the agreement takes effect between them on 1 July 2025. This means judgments from courts in one place can be recognised and enforced in the other, making cross-border cases cheaper, faster and more predictable. The Parliament also says the EU should follow its formal treaty procedure when third countries ask to join such agreements. This resolution states a position; it does not itself change any law.

- The UK joins the judgments agreement with the EU from 1 July 2025, if the EU accepts.
- People and businesses involved in cross-border civil or commercial disputes benefit.
- The EU Commission and Council now decide whether to accept the UK's accession.
